title: Nelson & Abel Tasman Tours: Kayaking, Water Taxis & Day Trips — WanderNewZealand
description: Tours from Nelson, Motueka, Kaiteriteri and Marahau into Abel Tasman National Park: sea kayaking, water taxis, coastal walks, helicopters and wine. Live operator prices.
hero: Sea kayaks, water taxis and coastal walks into Abel Tasman National Park, plus helicopters, wineries and mountain-bike trails out of Nelson.
intro: Nelson is the northern tip of the South Island and the gateway to three national parks. Abel Tasman is the one most visitors come for: a coastal track of golden beaches and estuaries with no road access past Marahau, so you get in by water taxi, by kayak, or on foot. The launch points are Marahau and Kaiteriteri, roughly an hour's drive west of Nelson past Motueka.

The classic pattern is a water taxi one way and a walk or paddle back. Water taxis run a fixed schedule up the coast and drop you at Anchorage, Bark Bay, Onetahuti or Awaroa; most people walk south for three to four hours and get collected. Guided kayak days cover the Astrolabe Roadstead and the seal colony on Tonga Island. If you have a full day, a kayak-and-walk combo does both.

Nelson itself has the Great Taste Trail cycle route through the Moutere wine country, the Nelson Lakes to the south, and helicopter operators who run Abel Tasman scenic flights and alpine landings. Golden Bay and Farewell Spit are a further two hours over the Tākaka Hill.
season_h2: Best time to go: November to March
season: Abel Tasman is a summer park. From November the water taxis move to their full timetable, the kayak operators run morning and afternoon departures, and sea temperatures climb to the high teens by January. December 26 to mid-January is the busiest fortnight of the year; book kayaks and water taxis a week or more ahead for those dates. November and March are the quieter ends of the season with the same daylight and most of the warmth.
Tides matter here: the Awaroa estuary crossing on the Coast Track is only passable within about two hours of low tide, so check tide times before booking a one-way walk that crosses it.
know: Marahau and Kaiteriteri are the launch points — about 60 minutes from Nelson by car or shuttle
No roads inside the park past Marahau; access is by water taxi, kayak or the Coast Track
Water taxis run to a schedule and drop/collect at named beaches — book the return leg
Awaroa estuary crossing is tide-limited (roughly ±2 hours of low tide)
Kayak tours are weather-dependent; operators reschedule for strong northerlies
Bring reef-safe sunscreen and a hat — there is little shade on the water
faq: Do I need a guide to kayak in Abel Tasman?

No. Operators hire kayaks to experienced paddlers for freedom trips, but most first-time visitors book a guided half-day or full-day because the guides read the sea conditions and handle the water-taxi logistics. Guided days usually include the Tonga Island seal colony.
How do I get from Nelson to Abel Tasman National Park?

Drive or take a shuttle west through Motueka to Marahau or Kaiteriteri, about 60 to 70 minutes. Several operators include Nelson pickup; otherwise book the shuttle separately and allow time for the first water taxi, which typically leaves around 9am.
Can you do Abel Tasman in one day from Nelson?
Yes. A water taxi up the coast at 9am, a three-to-four-hour walk back to Anchorage or Marahau, and a shuttle home is a standard day trip. Kayak-and-walk combos also fit in a day if you start early.
Is the water warm enough to swim?
In summer, yes. Sea temperatures reach 18 to 20°C from January to March. In November it is closer to 15°C — fine for a dip, cool for a long swim.

title: Christchurch Tours: Akaroa Dolphins, Banks Peninsula, Punting & Day Trips — WanderNewZealand
description: Christchurch and Banks Peninsula tours: Akaroa harbour cruises, Hector's dolphin swims, Pōhatu penguins, kayaking, city tours and Arthur's Pass day trips. Live operator prices.
hero: Punting on the Avon, Hector's dolphins at Akaroa, penguins on Banks Peninsula, and the TranzAlpine corridor into the Southern Alps.
intro: Christchurch is the South Island's largest city and the arrival point for most travellers heading to Kaikōura, Aoraki/Mount Cook or the West Coast. The city has rebuilt around the Avon River, Hagley Park and the new Riverside precinct, and the tour scene reflects that: punting, tram tours, guided walks of the post-earthquake architecture, and street-art bike rides.

Banks Peninsula, 80 minutes south-east, is where the wildlife is. Akaroa Harbour is a drowned volcanic crater and home to Hector's dolphins, the world's smallest marine dolphin; harbour cruises and dolphin swims run daily from the Akaroa wharf in summer. Over the hill at Flea Bay, the Pōhatu white-flippered penguin colony is visited by 4WD and sea-kayak safaris that leave from Akaroa village.

Inland, the Waimakariri Gorge jetboats and the Castle Hill limestone are an hour out on the Arthur's Pass road, and day trips to Lake Tekapo and Mount Cook run from the city for those not hiring a car.
season_h2: Best time to go: November to March
season: Summer is when Akaroa works best. Hector's dolphins are in the harbour year-round but come closer inshore from November to March, and the swim-with-dolphins permits are capped per boat, so those trips sell out first. Penguin numbers at Pōhatu peak during the September-to-February breeding season; by late February the adults are moulting and sightings drop.
Christchurch's nor'wester can shut down Akaroa boat trips at short notice. Most operators will move you to the next available departure, so leave a spare morning if a dolphin swim is the priority.
know: Akaroa is 80 minutes from the city — many wildlife tours include Christchurch pickup
Dolphin swim permits limit numbers per boat; book ahead for December–February
Pōhatu penguin tours leave from Akaroa village, not the wharf — check the meeting point
The nor'wester cancels harbour trips; keep a spare morning
Punting and tram tours run from the central city year-round
Arthur's Pass and Castle Hill are a day trip; Mount Cook is a long one (5 hours each way)
faq: Can you swim with dolphins in Christchurch?

Not in the city, but at Akaroa on Banks Peninsula, 80 minutes away. Licensed operators run swims with Hector's dolphins from the Akaroa wharf; wetsuits and snorkels are supplied and numbers in the water are capped by permit.
What is the best day trip from Christchurch?

Akaroa for wildlife (dolphins, penguins, harbour cruise), Arthur's Pass or Castle Hill for alpine scenery, Kaikōura for whales (2.5 hours north). Lake Tekapo and Aoraki/Mount Cook are possible in a long day but better as an overnight.
How far is Akaroa from Christchurch?
About 75 km, 1 hour 20 minutes by road over the Hilltop. Several operators include return transfers from central Christchurch hotels.
When do the penguins come ashore at Pōhatu?
Through the breeding season from roughly September to February. Evening tours time arrival for the birds returning after dark; daytime tours visit the nest boxes and the marine reserve.

title: Dunedin Tours: Otago Peninsula Albatross, Penguins, Wildlife Cruises & Larnach Castle — WanderNewZealand
description: Dunedin and Otago Peninsula tours: royal albatross colony, yellow-eyed and little blue penguins, wildlife cruises, Larnach Castle, Speight's and Taieri Gorge. Live operator prices.
hero: The only mainland royal albatross colony in the world, yellow-eyed penguins on the Otago Peninsula, and a Victorian city built on gold.
intro: Dunedin is the South Island's wildlife capital. The Otago Peninsula, which curls east from the city, holds the Royal Albatross Centre at Taiaroa Head — the only place on a mainland anywhere that northern royal albatross breed — plus colonies of yellow-eyed penguins (hoiho), little blue penguins, New Zealand fur seals and sea lions. Half-day and full-day wildlife tours cover the peninsula by minibus with stops at private conservation reserves you cannot reach on your own.

On the water, wildlife cruises leave from the Otago Harbour and Wellers Rock and run out past the albatross cliffs to where the birds take off and land; from November the season's chicks are on the nests and adults are commuting constantly. Back in the city, the Edwardian railway station, Speight's brewery, the Baldwin Street climb and Larnach Castle fill the tour calendar.
Dunedin is also the jumping-off point for the Catlins coast to the south and the Central Otago rail trail inland.
season_h2: Best time to go: November to March
season: Albatross activity at Taiaroa Head is highest from November through February, when the parents are feeding chicks and the wind is reliable enough for the big birds to fly. Yellow-eyed penguin chicks hatch in November and the adults come ashore every evening to feed them through January; evening tours are timed to that. Little blue penguins are viewable year-round at Pilots Beach.
Dunedin summer days are long (sunset after 9:30pm in December) and the weather is cooler than the north — bring a jacket for the peninsula even in January; the albatross cliffs are exposed.
know: Otago Peninsula tours are 40–60 minutes from the city centre by minibus; most include pickup
Albatross chicks are on the nest from late January; flying adults are most active in summer wind
Yellow-eyed penguin viewing is from hides at dusk — evening tours run late in summer
Wildlife cruises depart from Wellers Rock and the city wharf; both pass Taiaroa Head
Sea lions haul out on Allans Beach and Sandfly Bay — keep 20 metres back
Cruise-ship days (Port Chalmers) fill tours — check the port schedule and book early
faq: Where can I see penguins in Dunedin?

Yellow-eyed penguins at private reserves on the Otago Peninsula (guided tours only), little blue penguins at Pilots Beach beside the Royal Albatross Centre, and both from the water on peninsula wildlife cruises. Evening tours give the best yellow-eyed sightings as the birds come ashore.
Can you see albatross from a boat in Dunedin?

Yes. Harbour and coastal wildlife cruises run past the Taiaroa Head cliffs where the royal albatross nest; on a windy afternoon you will see adults landing and taking off. The land-based Royal Albatross Centre tour gets you inside the observatory.
How long should I spend on the Otago Peninsula?
A half-day covers the albatross centre or a wildlife cruise; a full day adds the yellow-eyed penguin reserves, Larnach Castle and the beaches. Most peninsula tours run 5 to 7 hours.
Is Dunedin a good base for the Catlins?
Yes. The Catlins coast (Nugget Point, Purakaunui Falls, Curio Bay) starts 90 minutes south and is a long day trip or a comfortable overnight loop back via Invercargill.

title: Wellington Tours: Zealandia, Harbour Cruises, Lord of the Rings & Food Tours — WanderNewZealand
description: Wellington tours: Zealandia ecosanctuary, harbour and Matiu/Somes Island cruises, Weta and Lord of the Rings location tours, craft beer and food walks, Kāpiti Island. Live operator prices.
hero: The capital on a harbour: Zealandia's kiwi, Weta Workshop, Middle-earth film locations, craft beer and the ferry to the South Island.
intro: Wellington is compact enough to walk and built on hills steep enough that most visitors don't. The waterfront, Te Papa, the Cable Car and Cuba Street are all within 20 minutes of each other on foot; the tour scene fills in what's harder to reach on your own — Zealandia's predator-free valley five minutes from downtown, Weta Workshop in Miramar, the Lord of the Rings locations scattered through the Hutt Valley and the town belt, and the islands in the harbour.

Harbour trips run to Matiu/Somes Island, a former quarantine station now managed as a reserve, and on calmer days out to the heads and the south coast seal colonies. Kayak and SUP hire operates from the waterfront. Food and craft-beer walking tours lean on the density of Wellington's bar and café scene; most run three hours and stop at four or five venues.
North of the city, Kāpiti Island is one of the country's most important bird sanctuaries and takes a permitted boat crossing from Paraparaumu, about 50 minutes up the coast.
season_h2: Best time to go: November to March
season: Wellington's wind is real, but summer is when the harbour is most often flat enough for kayaks, SUPs and the Somes Island ferry to run every scheduled sailing. Zealandia's night tours — the best way to see a kiwi in the wild — run year-round but start later in summer (around 9pm in December) because of the long twilight. Kāpiti Island crossings are most reliable from November onwards.
Late February to early March hosts the Fringe Festival and CubaDupa; accommodation tightens and walking tours book out on the weekends.
know: Zealandia is 10 minutes from the CBD by free shuttle from the i-SITE; night tours need booking
Weta Workshop tours are in Miramar — 20 minutes by bus or included in film-location tours
Somes Island ferries run from Queens Wharf; last return sailing is mid-afternoon
Kāpiti Island requires a licensed operator; check the sea-state cancellation policy
The Interislander and Bluebridge ferries to Picton leave from different terminals
Wind cancellations are common for harbour kayaking — operators reschedule freely
faq: Can you see a kiwi in Wellington?

Yes — Zealandia's night tour is the most reliable wild kiwi sighting in any New Zealand city. Little spotted kiwi were reintroduced to the fenced valley and are heard, and usually seen, on most evening tours.
Which Lord of the Rings locations are near Wellington?

Mount Victoria (the hobbits hiding from the Nazgûl), the Hutt River (Anduin), Kaitoke Regional Park (Rivendell) and Harcourt Park (Isengard gardens). Half-day and full-day tours cover the town-belt sites and the Hutt Valley; most add a Weta Workshop visit.
Is Matiu/Somes Island worth visiting?

For a half-day, yes. The ferry takes 20 minutes, the island loop walk is about an hour, and you will see tuatara, weta and little blue penguins depending on the season. Take food; there is nothing to buy on the island.
How do I get to Kāpiti Island?

By licensed boat from Paraparaumu Beach, 50 minutes north of Wellington by train or car. Day permits are included with the operator booking; the crossing is 15 minutes and sailings depend on the swell.

title: Wānaka & Cardrona Tours: Skydiving, Lake Cruises, Mount Aspiring, Heli & Horse Treks — WanderNewZealand
description: Wānaka and Cardrona tours: skydiving, Mount Aspiring heli flights, Lake Wānaka cruises and kayaks, Rob Roy and Blue Pools guided walks, Cardrona horse treks and the Wānaka tree. Live operator prices.
hero: Queenstown's quieter neighbour: Lake Wānaka, Mount Aspiring National Park, Cardrona Valley horse treks and the highest-rated skydive in the South Island.
intro: Wānaka sits an hour north-east of Queenstown over the Crown Range, on the southern shore of its own lake with Mount Aspiring National Park filling the western horizon. It has the same adventure menu as Queenstown — skydiving, canyoning, jetboats, heli-flights, lake cruises — at roughly half the crowd. The town centre is a single lakefront strip; most operator pickups are from the i-SITE or the lakefront car park.

Mount Aspiring is the draw for walkers and flyers. Guided day walks go up the Matukituki Valley to the Rob Roy Glacier viewpoint; helicopter operators land on the glaciers around Tititea/Mount Aspiring itself; and the Blue Pools and Haast Pass are a 70-minute drive north for a half-day. Lake cruises run to Mou Waho Island, which has its own lake on top with an island in it.
Cardrona, 25 minutes up the Crown Range road, is a ski field in winter and in summer a mountain-bike park and horse-trekking valley with the historic Cardrona Hotel at the bottom.
season_h2: Best time to go: November to March
season: Summer is the walking and lake season. The Matukituki Valley road to the Rob Roy track is unsealed with fords that are usually passable from November; guided walks handle the river crossings. Skydives and heli-flights run year-round but have the clearest air and longest operating windows in summer, with sunrise flights from about 6am in December. Lake water reaches 18 to 20°C by late January.
Cardrona's summer trails and horse treks open from around Labour Weekend (late October) and run to Easter. Early January is peak; late February and March are drier and quieter.
know: Wānaka is 60–70 minutes from Queenstown via the Crown Range (steep; chains in winter only)
Skydive and heli operators meet at Wānaka Airport, 10 minutes east of town
Rob Roy Glacier walk: 3–4 hours return, 50-minute gravel drive from town — guided tours include transport
Lake cruises and kayak hire leave from the lakefront by the i-SITE
Cardrona horse treks and bike park are 25 minutes up the Crown Range road
Alpine weather changes fast — wear layers for anything above the valley floor
faq: Is Wānaka or Queenstown better for skydiving?

Both are world-renowned drop zones and both have excellent safety records. Wānaka's selling point is the view: Mount Aspiring, Lake Wānaka and Lake Hāwea from 15,000 feet, with fewer other aircraft in the sky. Queenstown's is the convenience if you are based there.
How do I get to the Rob Roy Glacier?

Drive 50 minutes up the Matukituki Valley on gravel (fords included) to Raspberry Creek car park, then walk 3–4 hours return. Guided walks from Wānaka include the drive and the river crossings, which is the sensible option without a 4WD.
Can you visit Cardrona in summer?
Yes. The ski field runs a summer mountain-bike park and chairlift from December to April; the Cardrona Valley has horse treks and the historic hotel year-round.
Where is the Wānaka tree?
On the lakeshore at the western end of Roys Bay, a 10-minute walk from the town centre along the lakefront path. Early morning is quietest.

title: Tauranga & Mount Maunganui Tours: Dolphins, Surfing, Glow-Worm Kayaks & Bay of Plenty — WanderNewZealand
description: Tauranga, Mount Maunganui and Papamoa tours: dolphin cruises, surf lessons, McLaren Falls glow-worm kayaking, Kaimai hikes, kiwifruit and Hobbiton day trips. Live operator prices.
hero: Bay of Plenty's beach town: Mauao at dawn, dolphins offshore, surf schools on the main beach and glow-worm kayaking after dark.
intro: Tauranga is the country's biggest export port and its fastest-growing city, but the visitor centre of gravity is Mount Maunganui — a beach suburb wrapped around Mauao, the 232-metre volcanic cone at the harbour entrance. The Mauao base track takes 45 minutes; the summit an hour. Below it, the main beach is one of the most consistent learner surf breaks in the North Island, and surf schools run from the sand.

Offshore, common and bottlenose dolphins work the Bay of Plenty most days, and wildlife cruises leave from Tauranga Bridge Marina and Salisbury Wharf. Inland, McLaren Falls Park has a glow-worm gully that kayak operators paddle after dark, and the Kaimai Range offers waterfall walks within 30 minutes. Hobbiton at Matamata is 50 minutes west and is a standard day trip from here.
Cruise ships berth at the Mount from October to April, which means the dolphin and Hobbiton tours fill on port days; check the schedule.
season_h2: Best time to go: November to March
season: The Mount is a summer beach town. Water temperature passes 20°C by January, surf schools run multiple sessions a day, and the dolphin operators go to daily departures. December 26 to the end of January is busiest — the Mount's population roughly triples — and the glow-worm kayak tours, which take small groups, sell out well ahead on those dates. November and March have the same water, less crowd.
Evening kayak tours start later in summer (around 8:30pm) to allow full dark for the glow-worms.
know: Mount Maunganui and Tauranga are 10 minutes apart across the harbour bridge
Dolphin cruises depart from Tauranga Bridge Marina — allow 4–5 hours
Surf lessons run from the main beach at the Mount; boards and wetsuits included
Glow-worm kayaking at McLaren Falls is 20 minutes inland and runs after dark
Hobbiton is 50 minutes west — several tours include Tauranga pickup
Cruise-ship days fill tours; book ahead for October–April port days
faq: Can you swim with dolphins in Tauranga?

Licensed wildlife cruises from Tauranga encounter common and bottlenose dolphins on most summer trips and, where conditions and permits allow, offer in-water time. Sightings are not guaranteed; most operators offer a return trip if none are seen.
Is Mount Maunganui good for learning to surf?
Yes — the main beach is a sandy-bottom beach break with gentle whitewater in the inside and schools operating from the sand with all gear supplied. Lessons run year-round; summer water is warmest.
Where is the glow-worm kayaking near Tauranga?
McLaren Falls Park, about 20 minutes south-west of the city, where guided kayak tours paddle Lake McLaren into a glow-worm canyon after dark. Tours run most evenings in summer and take small groups.
How far is Hobbiton from Tauranga?
About 55 km to Matamata, 50 minutes by road. Hobbiton tours with Tauranga hotel or cruise-terminal pickup are widely available.

title: Taupō Tours: Huka Falls Jet, Lake Cruises, Māori Rock Carvings, Skydiving & Tongariro — WanderNewZealand
description: Taupō and Tūrangi tours: Huka Falls jetboat, Māori rock carvings by boat or kayak, skydiving over the lake, Tongariro Alpine Crossing shuttles, trout fishing and geothermal walks. Live operator prices.
hero: New Zealand's largest lake: Huka Falls by jetboat, the Mine Bay rock carvings by kayak, skydives from 15,000 feet and the Tongariro Alpine Crossing an hour south.
intro: Lake Taupō is the flooded caldera of one of the largest volcanic eruptions in recorded history, and the town on its north shore is the North Island's adventure hub. Huka Falls — the full Waikato River forced through a 15-metre gap — is five minutes from town and the jetboat trips run right up to the base of it. Skydiving over the lake, with Mount Ruapehu and the central plateau behind, is the other signature trip.

On the water, the Ngātoroirangi Mine Bay rock carvings are only reachable by boat; sailing yachts, launches and guided kayak tours leave from the Taupō boat harbour and take two to four hours for the round trip. The lake's rainbow trout fishery supports guided fly-fishing and trolling charters year-round.

Tūrangi, 50 minutes south at the bottom of the lake, is the base for the Tongariro Alpine Crossing shuttles and the Tongariro River rafting runs. Orakei Korako and Wairakei geothermal areas are 20 to 30 minutes north.
season_h2: Best time to go: November to March
season: Summer brings the lake up to swimming temperature (around 20°C by February), reliable flying weather for skydives and scenic flights, and the start of the main Tongariro Alpine Crossing season — from about Labour Weekend the track is usually snow-free and the shuttle operators run their full timetable. Kayak trips to the carvings are at their calmest in the mornings; afternoon westerlies pick up on the open lake.
The Ironman in early March and school holidays from late December fill accommodation; tour availability holds up but book the small-group kayak trips a few days ahead.
know: Huka Falls is 5 minutes from town; jetboat trips leave from Wairakei Tourist Park
The Mine Bay rock carvings are boat-access only — 2 hours by launch, 4 by kayak
Skydive operators meet at Taupō Airport, 10 minutes south
Tongariro Alpine Crossing shuttles leave from Tūrangi and Taupō before dawn; 19.4 km one way
Afternoon westerlies make the open lake rough — kayak tours go in the morning
Trout fishing needs a Taupō Fishing District licence (operators arrange it)
faq: How do you get to the Māori rock carvings at Lake Taupō?

By water only. Scenic cruises and sailing trips from the Taupō boat harbour take about 2 hours; guided kayak tours from Acacia Bay paddle there and back in 3 to 4 hours and get closest to the carvings.
Can you do the Tongariro Alpine Crossing from Taupō?
Yes. Shuttle operators pick up in Taupō and Tūrangi before dawn, drop at Mangatepopo and collect at Ketetahi. The 19.4 km crossing takes 6 to 8 hours; the main season is late October to April.
Is skydiving in Taupō good?

Taupō is the busiest drop zone in New Zealand for a reason: the view takes in the whole lake, the three central-plateau volcanoes and, on clear days, Mount Taranaki. Jumps run from 12,000 and 15,000 feet year-round, weather permitting.
What is the best way to see Huka Falls?

Walk the free viewing platform first (5 minutes from the car park), then take a jetboat if you want to be at the base of it — the Hukafalls Jet runs up the river from Wairakei every 30 minutes in summer.

title: Fiordland & Te Anau Tours: Milford Sound, Doubtful Sound, Glowworm Caves & Heli Flights — WanderNewZealand
description: Fiordland tours from Te Anau and Manapouri: Milford Sound and Doubtful Sound cruises, Te Anau glowworm caves, helicopter landings, Kepler and Routeburn day walks, jet boats on the Waiau. Live operator prices.
hero: The gateway town for Milford and Doubtful Sounds: glowworm caves across the lake, heli-flights over the fiords, and the start of the Kepler and Milford Tracks.
intro: Te Anau is the town on the edge of Fiordland National Park and the sensible base for seeing both of the famous fiords without a 12-hour day from Queenstown. Milford Sound is 118 km up the Milford Road — two hours' drive, more with stops at Mirror Lakes, the Homer Tunnel and the Chasm. Doubtful Sound is reached from Manapouri, 20 minutes south, via a boat across Lake Manapouri and a bus over Wilmot Pass.

Te Anau's own attractions are the glowworm caves — a boat trip across the lake to a limestone cave system — and the start points of the Kepler Track (walkable as a day loop to the Luxmore Hut) and, via the Milford Road, the Routeburn and Milford Tracks. Helicopter operators based at Te Anau fly over the fiords, land on Mount Luxmore and reach Dusky Sound, which no road touches.
Everything here is further than it looks. Bus-and-cruise combinations from Te Anau remove the driving and are the standard way to do Milford in a day.
season_h2: Best time to go: November to March
season: The Great Walks season — Milford, Routeburn, Kepler — opens in late October and runs to the end of April; this is when huts are serviced, bridges are in and the Milford Road is reliably open without avalanche closures. Day-cruise departures to both fiords move to their summer timetable in November, with the first Milford cruises leaving around 9am and the last in mid-afternoon. December to February is peak; November and March have the same daylight with easier bookings.
Fiordland gets 7 metres of rain a year and the waterfalls are at their best the day after a downpour. Bring a proper rain jacket in every month, and sandfly repellent from November on.
know: Milford Sound is 2 hours from Te Anau by car — coach-cruise packages include the drive
Doubtful Sound trips leave from Manapouri (20 min south): boat, bus over Wilmot Pass, then cruise
Te Anau glowworm caves are a 2-hour evening or afternoon trip across the lake
Great Walks huts book out months ahead in summer; day walks on the Kepler need no booking
Heli-flights to Dusky Sound and Mount Luxmore weather-dependent — allow a spare morning
Sandflies are serious here from November — repellent, long sleeves
faq: Should I stay in Te Anau or Queenstown for Milford Sound?

Te Anau if Milford is the priority. It cuts the return drive from about 8 hours (Queenstown) to 4, lets you take a morning cruise before the coach crowds, and puts Doubtful Sound and the glowworm caves within reach on other days.
Can you do both Milford and Doubtful Sound from Te Anau?

Yes, on consecutive days. Milford is a day trip up the Milford Road; Doubtful Sound is a separate full day from Manapouri. The two cannot be combined in one day by road — see our Milford vs Doubtful guide for how they differ.
How far is it from Milford Sound to Doubtful Sound?

About 40 km apart as the crow flies, but there is no road between them. By car it is roughly 4 hours back via Te Anau to Manapouri, then the lake crossing and Wilmot Pass bus. Helicopter is the only direct route.
Are the Te Anau glowworm caves worth it?

Yes if you have an evening free. The trip is a 30-minute lake crossing, a guided walk into the Aurora cave system and a short boat ride in the dark under the glowworms, about 2 hours 15 minutes in total.

title: Kaikōura Tours: Whale Watching, Dolphin Swims, Seal Kayaking & Albatross — WanderNewZealand
description: Kaikōura tours: sperm whale watching by boat and air, dusky dolphin swims, fur seal kayaking, albatross encounters, crayfish and coastal walks. Live operator prices.
hero: Sperm whales a few kilometres offshore year-round, dusky dolphins in pods of hundreds, and fur seals you can paddle a kayak past.
intro: Kaikōura sits where the Seaward Kaikōura Range drops into the Pacific and a 1,000-metre-deep submarine canyon runs almost to the beach. That canyon is why resident sperm whales feed here all year within a 20-minute boat ride of the harbour, and why Kaikōura built a whole town's economy on watching them. Whale trips run by catamaran from South Bay and by fixed-wing aircraft and helicopter from the airfield.

Dusky dolphins are the other headline. Pods of several hundred live off the peninsula and the swim-with-dolphins operators put you in the water with them on early-morning trips; wetsuits and snorkels are supplied. New Zealand fur seals haul out at Point Kean on the peninsula walkway and along the coast north of town, and guided sea-kayak trips paddle along the colony at close range.
Kaikōura is 2.5 hours north of Christchurch and 2 hours south of Blenheim on State Highway 1, with the Coastal Pacific train stopping in summer.
season_h2: Best time to go: November to March
season: Sperm whales are resident, so whale watching is good year-round; summer adds calmer seas, fewer cancellations and, from December, the chance of orca, blue and humpback whales passing through. Dusky dolphin swims run all year but the water is warmest (16–18°C) from January to March, and the dolphins are most inshore in summer. Seal pups are on the rocks from December; kayak trips keep the required distance but you will see plenty.

Early-morning departures (6:30–7:30am) have the flattest sea and the best chance of a full trip. Afternoon trips in summer can be cancelled by the sea breeze — book the morning and keep the afternoon free.
know: Whale watching leaves from South Bay (boat) or the airfield (plane/heli), both 5 minutes from town
Boat trips are 3–3.5 hours; seasickness tablets are worth taking
Dolphin swims are early morning — wetsuits, masks and snorkels supplied
Seal kayaking paddles past the Point Kean colony; no experience needed
The peninsula walkway (3 hours) is free and passes the main seal haul-out
SH1 north and south can close in heavy rain — check before a day trip from Christchurch
faq: What is the best time of year to see whales in Kaikōura?

Sperm whales are here every month, so any time works. December to March adds calmer seas and migrating humpbacks and orca; June to August is the season for the largest sperm whale bulls. Morning trips have the best conditions.
Can you swim with dolphins in Kaikōura?

Yes. Licensed operators run early-morning trips to swim with dusky dolphins in the open sea; pods often number in the hundreds. Snorkelling ability is required; wetsuits are supplied and numbers in the water are limited by permit.
How far is Kaikōura from Christchurch?
About 180 km, 2.5 hours by road on SH1, or 3 hours on the Coastal Pacific train (summer timetable). It works as a long day trip but an overnight gives you the morning dolphin swim.
Is whale watching by boat or by plane better?

The boat gets you close to the whale at the surface and lasts 3 hours; the plane sees the whole animal underwater from above and takes 30 to 40 minutes. The boat is more affected by swell; the plane by cloud.

title: Bay of Islands Tours: Hole in the Rock, Dolphin Cruises, Waitangi, Kayaking & Cape Reinga — WanderNewZealand
description: Bay of Islands tours from Paihia and Russell: Hole in the Rock cruises, dolphin watching, guided kayaking to Haruru Falls, Waitangi Treaty Grounds, Cape Reinga and Ninety Mile Beach day trips. Live operator prices.
hero: 144 islands, the Hole in the Rock, bottlenose dolphins, and the place New Zealand's founding treaty was signed — all from Paihia wharf.
intro: The Bay of Islands is three hours north of Auckland and the warmest sailing water in the country. Paihia is the operator town — the wharf is where the Hole in the Rock cruises, dolphin trips, island-hopping ferries and sailing charters all leave — and Russell, across the water by passenger ferry, is the quieter historic village. Waitangi Treaty Grounds, a 20-minute walk from Paihia, is where the 1840 treaty between Māori and the Crown was signed.

The Hole in the Rock at Cape Brett is the standard half-day: a fast catamaran or a sailing boat out through the islands, through the rock arch if the swell allows, with dolphins on most trips. Guided kayak tours paddle the Waitangi River up to Haruru Falls, one of the few waterfalls in the country you can kayak behind, and night kayaks in summer go for the bioluminescence.
Cape Reinga and Ninety Mile Beach are a long full-day coach trip north (about 12 hours return) and are run from Paihia daily in summer.
season_h2: Best time to go: November to March
season: Northland's season starts earlier than the South Island's. By November the water is 19°C and the Hole in the Rock boats are on their full timetable; by February it is 22°C and swimming stops off the boats are routine. Bottlenose dolphins are resident and seen most of the year; common dolphins and, occasionally, orca are summer visitors. The Cape Reinga coach runs daily from November with a sand-dune boarding stop.

Waitangi Day (6 February) brings crowds and ceremonies to the Treaty Grounds; it is a good day to be there and a bad day to need a last-minute booking. Christmas to mid-January is busiest on the water.
know: Paihia wharf is the departure point for almost everything; Russell is a 15-minute passenger ferry
Hole in the Rock cruises take 4–5 hours; passage through the arch depends on swell
Dolphin swimming is no longer permitted in the Bay — watching only, by DOC rule
Waitangi Treaty Grounds is a 20-minute walk from Paihia; allow 2–3 hours
Cape Reinga day trips are 12 hours return — leave before 7:30am
Kayak tours to Haruru Falls are tide-dependent on the Waitangi River
faq: Can you swim with dolphins in the Bay of Islands?

No. The Department of Conservation ended in-water dolphin encounters in the Bay of Islands in 2019 to protect the declining bottlenose population. Cruises still watch dolphins from the boat on most trips.
How long is the Hole in the Rock cruise?
Most Hole in the Rock trips from Paihia run 4 to 5 hours, including an island stop. The boat passes through the rock arch at Cape Brett only when the swell allows; otherwise it circles close.
Is the Bay of Islands a day trip from Auckland?
It can be — about 3 hours each way plus a half-day cruise makes a 12-hour day. Two nights in Paihia is the usual recommendation, especially if you want Cape Reinga as well.
Can you kayak behind Haruru Falls?
Yes. Guided kayak tours paddle up the Waitangi River estuary and, at the right tide and river level, behind the curtain of the 5-metre horseshoe falls.

title: Doubtful Sound Cruises: Day Trips & Overnight Cruises from Manapouri, Te Anau & Queenstown — WanderNewZealand
description: Doubtful Sound cruise options compared: day wilderness cruises, one- and two-night overnight cruises, departures from Manapouri, Te Anau and Queenstown, plus helicopter access. Live operator prices.
hero: Three times the size of Milford, a tenth of the boats. Day cruises and overnight boats from Manapouri, with coach connections from Te Anau and Queenstown.
intro: Doubtful Sound has no road. Every trip starts with a 50-minute boat across Lake Manapouri, then a coach over the 671-metre Wilmot Pass — the most expensive road in New Zealand per kilometre, built for the power station — to Deep Cove, where the cruise vessel waits. That two-stage approach is why Doubtful takes a full day and why it sees a fraction of Milford's traffic.

Day cruises spend about three hours on the fiord, running the 40 km out to the Tasman Sea past the Shelter Islands fur seal colony and, in season, the bottlenose dolphin pod that lives in the sound. Total time from Manapouri is around 7 hours; from Te Anau add 40 minutes each way, from Queenstown add about 2.5 hours each way by coach.

Overnight cruises are the way most people who have done both fiords would choose to see Doubtful. The boats anchor in a side arm for the night, put kayaks and tender boats in the water in the evening, and run the sound in the early morning before the day boats arrive. One-night and two-night options exist, with private cabins or quad-share bunks.
season_h2: Best time to cruise: November to March
season: Overnight cruises run from roughly September to May and are busiest from mid-December through February, when the private cabins book out weeks ahead; shoulder months (November, March) have the same 15-hour daylight and more availability. Day cruises run year-round. Summer brings the dolphins into the inner arms more often and makes the evening kayaking off the overnight boats comfortable.
Rain is part of the deal in Fiordland — about 200 days a year — and the fiord is at its most dramatic the morning after a wet night, when hundreds of temporary waterfalls run off the walls.
know: All trips go via Lake Manapouri and Wilmot Pass — there is no road to the fiord
Day cruise: ~7 hours from Manapouri, ~8 from Te Anau, ~12 from Queenstown
Overnight cruises include dinner, breakfast, kayaks and tender-boat trips
Private cabins sell out first in summer; quad-share bunks are the budget option
Pack for rain and sandflies in every month
Cellphone coverage ends at Manapouri
faq: Can you do both Milford and Doubtful Sound?

Yes, but on separate days — there is no road between them and each is a full day. Base yourself in Te Anau and do Milford one day (2 hours each way by road) and Doubtful the next (via Manapouri). Combining both in one day is only possible by helicopter.
How far is Milford Sound from Doubtful Sound?

Roughly 40 km in a straight line, but there is no road link. By road it is about 4 hours from Milford back through Te Anau to Manapouri, then the lake boat and Wilmot Pass coach. Scenic flights cover it in under 30 minutes.
Is Doubtful Sound better than Milford Sound?

Different, not better. Milford has the single most dramatic view (Mitre Peak) and is a day trip from Queenstown; Doubtful is three times larger, far quieter, takes longer to reach and rewards an overnight. If you can only do one and are short on time, Milford; if you have a spare day, Doubtful overnight.
How much do Doubtful Sound cruises cost?

Day wilderness cruises from Manapouri start in the mid-NZ$300s per adult; add coach connections for Te Anau or Queenstown departures. Overnight cruises range from quad-share bunks to private en-suite cabins — check live prices on the cards above.
What is the Dusky Sound cruise?
Dusky Sound is the next fiord south and has no scheduled day boats; it is reached by multi-day expedition cruise or by helicopter from Te Anau. Prices reflect the remoteness.

title: Fiordland Cruises: Milford Sound, Doubtful Sound & Overnight Cruise Prices Compared — WanderNewZealand
description: Every Fiordland cruise in one place: Milford Sound day cruises, Doubtful Sound wilderness cruises, one- and two-night overnight cruises, coach-cruise and fly-cruise-fly packages from Queenstown and Te Anau. Live prices in NZ$.
hero: Milford and Doubtful Sound day cruises, overnight boats, and the coach and flight combinations that get you there from Queenstown and Te Anau — with live prices.
intro: Fiordland National Park has fourteen fiords and two with scheduled cruises: Milford Sound and Doubtful Sound. Milford is the famous one — Mitre Peak, Stirling Falls, a 16 km run to the sea — and has the widest choice of boats, from 2-hour nature cruises to small-boat and overnight options. Doubtful is larger, quieter and reached only via Lake Manapouri and Wilmot Pass, which makes it a longer day and a stronger case for staying the night on board.

Prices depend less on the boat than on how you reach it. A Milford Sound cruise alone is the cheapest line on this page; add a coach from Te Anau and it roughly doubles; add a coach from Queenstown and the day becomes 12 hours; replace the return coach with a scenic flight (coach-cruise-fly) or fly both ways (fly-cruise-fly) and you are into the premium bracket but back in Queenstown by early afternoon.

Overnight cruises on either fiord include dinner, breakfast, kayaking and tender trips and anchor in arms the day boats never reach. For multi-day expedition cruising into Dusky, Breaksea and the southern fiords, a handful of small vessels run 3- to 7-night itineraries in summer.
season: Day cruises run every day of the year; what changes in summer is frequency and daylight. From November, Milford operators run departures roughly hourly from 9am to 3pm, overnight boats are on their full schedule, and the Milford Road is open without avalanche-control closures. Fly-cruise-fly and coach-cruise-fly packages depend on Milford airstrip weather and are most reliable from December to March.
Book overnight cabins and anything departing between 24 December and 31 January as early as you can; day cruises from Milford itself rarely sell out, but the coaches from Queenstown do.
know: Milford Sound: 2 hours from Te Anau, 4 from Queenstown by road — cruise alone is 1.5–2.5 hours
Doubtful Sound: via Manapouri lake crossing + Wilmot Pass coach — about 7 hours total
Coach-cruise-fly and fly-cruise-fly packages cut the Queenstown day from 12 hours to 4–6
Overnight cruises include meals, kayaks and tender boats; cabins book out in summer
Prices shown are per adult in NZ$ where the operator publishes a per-person rate
Flights are weather-dependent; the coach is the fallback on cloudy days
faq: How much does a Fiordland cruise cost?

A Milford Sound day cruise alone starts around NZ$130–200 per adult. Coach-and-cruise from Te Anau is roughly NZ$250–400; from Queenstown NZ$290–520. Fly-cruise-fly from Queenstown runs NZ$700–900. Doubtful Sound day cruises from Manapouri are mid-NZ$300s; overnight cruises on either fiord start around NZ$600–750 per person in shared cabins and more for private cabins. Live prices are on the cards above.
Milford Sound or Doubtful Sound — which cruise should I pick?
Milford for the iconic view and a day trip from Queenstown; Doubtful for scale, quiet and an overnight. Our Milford vs Doubtful guide breaks it down.
Are there multi-day Fiordland cruises?

Yes — one- and two-night overnight cruises on Milford and Doubtful Sound run most of the year, and a few expedition vessels offer 3- to 7-night itineraries into Dusky and Breaksea Sounds in summer. The expedition trips are small-group and priced accordingly.
Can you cruise Fiordland from Queenstown in a day?
Yes. Coach-cruise-coach to Milford is a 12-hour day; coach-cruise-fly is 8–9 hours; fly-cruise-fly about 4 hours. Doubtful Sound from Queenstown by coach is 12–13 hours.
What is the difference between a Milford Sound nature cruise and a scenic cruise?

Nature cruises are usually smaller boats, 2–2.5 hours, with more commentary and closer approaches to the walls and wildlife. Scenic cruises are the larger vessels on 1.5–2 hour loops. Both reach the Tasman Sea entrance in normal conditions.

title: Jet Ski Hire Auckland: Rentals & Guided Jet Ski Tours on the Hauraki Gulf — WanderNewZealand
description: Jet ski hire and rentals in Auckland and Whangaparāoa: 30-minute to full-day hire, guided jet ski tours on the Hauraki Gulf, licence rules, prices in NZ$ and what is included. Live operator prices.
hero: Hire a jet ski by the half-hour or the day on the Hauraki Gulf, from the city waterfront and the Whangaparāoa Peninsula.
intro: Auckland has more boats per head than any city on earth and the Hauraki Gulf to use them on — 1.2 million hectares of sheltered water, dozens of islands and, in summer, flat mornings that suit a jet ski. Hire operates from two bases: the city waterfront and the Whangaparāoa Peninsula 40 minutes north, where the Hibiscus Coast beaches give direct access to the gulf and the Tiritiri Matangi channel.

Rental works by time block, from 30 minutes up to a full six hours, and the hourly rate drops the longer you take. Machines are current-model three-seat skis; life jackets, a safety briefing and a marked riding area or route are included, and you do not need a boat licence in New Zealand. Riders must be 16 or older to drive; passengers younger than that ride with an adult. Guided tours — an operator-led ride out to the islands — run on request for groups and for first-timers who would rather not navigate.
Fuel is included in most hire blocks; check the deposit and the wind policy, since operators will not send skis out in a strong southwesterly.
season_h2: Best time to ride: November to March
season: Jet ski hire in Auckland is a summer business. Operators open their full timetable from Labour Weekend and run daily from November to Easter, weather allowing; water temperature reaches 20–22°C by January. Mornings are glassier than afternoons, when the sea breeze gets up across the gulf, so book early blocks for longer rides to the islands.

December 26 to the end of January is peak — weekends and the long holiday fortnight book out several days ahead. Weekday mornings in November, February and March have the same water and the best availability.
know: No licence needed to drive a jet ski in New Zealand; drivers must be 16+
Hire blocks run 30 minutes to 6 hours; longer blocks have a lower hourly rate
Fuel, life jackets and briefing included — check the security deposit
Whangaparāoa base is 40 minutes north of the CBD; city base on the waterfront
Operators cancel in strong wind — morning blocks are calmer
Three-seat skis: one driver plus up to two passengers
faq: Do you need a licence to hire a jet ski in Auckland?

No. New Zealand has no boat or jet ski licence requirement for recreational craft. Hire operators require drivers to be at least 16, give a safety briefing, and follow Auckland Council's 5-knot rule within 200 metres of shore and 50 metres of swimmers.
How much does jet ski hire cost in Auckland?
Roughly NZ$120–160 for 30 minutes, NZ$240 for an hour and under NZ$900 for a full 6-hour day, per ski (not per person) — see live prices on the cards above. Longer blocks work out cheaper per hour.
Where can you jet ski in Auckland?

From the Whangaparāoa Peninsula you ride the open Hauraki Gulf toward Tiritiri Matangi and the Noises; from the city waterfront, the inner harbour and out to Rangitoto. Operators mark a riding area or set a route for guided tours.
Can two people ride one jet ski?
Yes — the hire skis are three-seaters, so one driver and up to two passengers. The price is per ski, which makes a shared hire the cheapest way to do it.
